content_record.title: historical-2026-flavonoid-from-vine-tea-selectively-clears-senescent-microglia-repairs-b6867533
content_record.editorial_body: Dihydromyricetin, a natural flavonoid, acts as a senomorphic in fibroblasts by boosting PRDX2 nuclear translocation for DNA repair, and as a senolytic in microglia by disrupting mitochondrial function—offering a dual mechanism to combat age-related decline. Three things to remember - Dihydromyricetin protects senescent fibroblasts from DNA damage and reduces SASP. - It promotes PRDX2 nuclear translocation to facilitate DNA repair in senescent cells. - In microglia with low PRDX2, it triggers apoptosis via mitochondrial impairment. Source This signal is based on The natural flavonoid dihydromyricetin targets senescent cells via PRDX2 and alleviates age-related diseases. from PubMed. Read the original report for full context. Health note: Preclinical findings in mice and cells; human efficacy and safety unproven.
